Botfall · Field Manual

Land. Build. Expand.

Your robots have touched down on a dusty alien world. This manual covers everything you need to run the colony: what each building does, how goods flow, how batteries and terrain shape your plans, and how to beat the rival.

The goal

Gather raw resources, turn them into better goods, build more robots and spread across the planet. Pick a mode before each game.

Versus

A rival colony lands at the far end of the map. Capture its Command Base to win. If it captures yours, you lose. A game runs about 20–40 minutes, longer on hilly maps.

Missions

Eight set challenges on hand-picked planets, each with its own goals and Easy, Normal and Hard levels. See Missions.

Colony

No rival and no clock. Build supply chains and spread out. Milestones pop up at 10, 25, 40, 60 and 80% of the land your bots can reach.

New-game settings

Map sizeSmall 30×42, Medium 40×56, Large 50×70 or Huge 60×84 tiles. Remembered separately for each mode.
TerrainFlat, Gentle, Rolling, Rugged or Mountainous. Rougher maps have more cliff levels and fewer passes between them.
ResourcesScarce to Abundant: how many resource fields there are, how big they are and how long each deposit lasts.
RivalEasy, Normal or Hard (Versus only). Harder rivals produce faster and attack sooner.
PlanetWith the same settings, a planet number always makes the same map. Tap New planet for a different one.

You start with 10 Workers, 5 Haulers, an Agribot, 4 Warbots (Versus) and a Command Base, sitting on a ring of road, holding 16 8 8 4 4 4 24.

Controls

DragMove the map.
Pinch or scrollZoom in and out.
TapInspect anything: a building, a bot, a resource or a rally flag. The panel that opens shows what it's doing and the buttons for it.
MinimapTop right. Tap or drag on it to jump anywhere. A flashing ring marks a building under attack. The × hides it, and the map button brings it back.
Top barYour goods (in storage plus finished goods waiting in buildings; hover over or tap a counter to see its name and what it's for), workers and how many are free, warbots, the clock (or land claimed in Colony), game speed 1×/2×/3×, and the pause menu.
Goal bannerTells you the next sensible step. Tap it to fold it away.
Bottom barBuild opens the build menu, Paths draws roads, Army gives orders to warbots (Versus), Base jumps to your Command Base.
MessagesTap one to jump to where it happened.

On a computer

On a wide screen the top bar is a single row, the tools sit in a small dock at the bottom and panels open on the right, so the map stays in view. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan (right-drag pans in every mode, even while laying roads) and click to select. While placing a building it follows the mouse: click to place it.

B · P · A · HBuild, Paths, Army, Base.
R · O · LPaths: lay roads, one-way arrows, traffic lights.
Arrows / WASDPan the map. + and − zoom.
1 · 2 · 3Game speed.
M · Space · EscMinimap on or off, pause, and back (close a panel, leave a mode, or open the pause menu).

Your first ten minutes

Tap Build, pick a building and tap a highlighted tile. Each card shows how many of that building you already have. Check the preview, then tap Build here or tap the same tile again. Placing a site is free, but Haulers bring its materials by road: tap the new site and press Lay road (or draw one yourself in Paths) to join it to the ring of road round your Command Base; free workers pave it in a few seconds. You can have six sites going at once.

  1. HarvesterNext to the teal stalk groves. The preview says how many groves are in reach; aim for plenty.
  2. QuarryBy the grey boulders. Its Stone becomes Cement, which goes into almost every building.
  3. Cement WorksNear your Command Base. It bakes Stone into Cement, your main building material (and roads). It stops at 40 Cement so it doesn't eat all your Stone; tap it to change the limit.
  4. Ore Mine and Crystal TapThe mine by the dark veins with glowing orange cracks, the tap by the violet crystals.
  5. SmelterTurns Ore and Fiber into Alloy, the backbone of everything advanced.
  6. Chip FabTurns Crystal and Alloy into Chips. Every new bot needs one.
  7. Bot FoundryBuilds the Workers and Warbots you order. Tap it and press +1 or +5. More workers means faster everything, so order a few early.
  8. Charging StationOnce you're working far from your Command Base, so bots don't walk all the way home to recharge.
  9. Bio FarmBeside the dark, furrowed fertile soil. Charging Stations burn Fuel, and the farm grows it. Your Agribot runs it.
  10. OutpostNear your border to claim more land, then run a road out to it and to everything you build there.

The supply chain

Cement is your main building material. Nearly every building costs Cement, and so does every road; a Cement Works bakes 2 Cement from each Stone. Only the Quarry (Fiber) and the Cement Works itself (raw Stone and Fiber) can be built without it, so you can always get going again.

Stock limits. Tap a production building to set when it stops: once you have that much of what it makes, it takes no more inputs and its worker goes off to other jobs until it's needed again. The Cement Works stops at 40 and the Asphalt Plant at 20 unless you change them; the rest keep going until you set a limit.

Everything flows from four raw resources, plus energy crops and oil for Fuel. Resources sit in separate fields with open ground between them. Haulers carry goods two at a time along your roads, so short, fast roads and enough Haulers keep the chain moving.

Deposits run out, and your landing zone only has a little of everything. Stalk groves can be replanted with a Grove Planter (new groves take about a minute to grow). For more Ore, Crystal and oil, push your border out with Outposts: richer fields sit just beyond your starting land, and contested ones (including an oil field) lie in the middle of the map.

Every building needs a clear tile on all sides, so leave gaps. Tap one of your buildings to set its priority, pause it or demolish it. Demolishing returns half the materials; cancelling a site returns everything delivered.

Robots and logistics

Your colony has two kinds of worker robot. Workers run buildings (one inside each production building), go out to cut, dig and mine resources for them, and build construction sites. Haulers move every good between buildings, and only on roads. The top bar shows your workers (and how many are free) and your haulers. The Bot Foundry builds more of both, and specialists: tap it and press +1 or +5 next to any type.

WorkerRuns buildings, gathers and builds. Goes anywhere, but crawls at 40% speed off the road, except while out gathering for its building.

HaulerCarries two goods at a time between buildings and storage. Only drives on roads: a building with no road gets nothing.

AgribotThe only bot that can run a Bio Farm or a Grove Planter.

PaverThe only bot that can run a Roadworks and lay asphalt.

Specialists have a small badge (amber crate, green leaf, yellow stripe) so you can tell them apart on the map. Every bot costs 1 Alloy and 1 Chip.

  • Keep a worker or two free to build. If raids or new buildings leave none, the game takes a worker off the least useful job and tells you. The fix is more workers from the Bot Foundry.
  • Enough Haulers. If goods pile up waiting for pickup, order more Haulers. If every Hauler is lost, workers carry goods slowly until the Foundry makes more.
  • Priority. Tap a building or site and choose Low, Normal or High. High-priority ones get workers, builders and deliveries first. Low ones are served last and lose their worker first when you run short. A badge on the map shows anything you've changed.
  • Pause a building to free its worker until you resume it.
  • Storage. Tap your Command Base or a Depot. Fill first makes haulers bring finished goods there before any other storage, even a closer one. Empty out takes nothing new and moves what it holds elsewhere, which is handy before demolishing it. Tap individual goods to stop that building keeping them.

Roads and traffic

Roads are the heart of your colony. Haulers only drive on roads, so every building and construction site needs a road joined to storage: the ring of road your Command Base sits on, or a Depot on the same network. A red road badge marks any building that has none, and the goal banner warns you. Workers can cross open ground, but slowly. Roads double every bot's speed.

Tap Paths and drag across open ground inside your border to plan a road. You pay its Cement at once: 1 Cement paves 5 tiles, and the same Cement builds your buildings, so every highway is a trade-off. Planned tiles show dashed until free workers pave them, about a second and a half per tile (three through resources), working out from the roads you already have so a new road is usable as it grows. Tap a planned tile to call it off and get its Cement back.

Dragging goes round resources; tap a boulder, grove, ore or crystal tile to clear it for a road at three times the Cement. Tap a road to remove it and get its Cement back. Every building keeps a side open for a road, and roads work on slopes too. Plan long, straight highways between your fields, factories and Depots: it's how goods move over long distances efficiently. A long highway is a project, so plan it early and keep a few workers free to pave it.

Road2× speed. Laid by you with Cement.
Asphalt2¾× speed. A Roadworks with a Paver upgrades every road within 7 tiles, using 1 Asphalt for every 4 tiles. Asphalt isn't refunded if you remove the road.
  • Queues. Bots don't drive through each other on roads: each waits behind the bot ahead of it going the same way. A slow bot (say, one with a flat battery) backs up everyone behind it, and so does a crowd at a busy building.
  • Two-way roads. Each direction keeps to its own side, so bots can pass, but passing oncoming traffic slows both down. A busy two-way road between storage and a factory backs up.
  • One-way roads. In the Paths banner, choose Arrows and drag along a road: each tile points the way you drag. Tap a road to turn its arrow (east, south, west, north, then two-way again). Choose Lay roads and drag over arrows to clear them.
  • Loops. Lay two one-way lanes side by side, or a ring around a busy area, so bots heading out and bots coming back never share a lane.
  • Bots can still go the wrong way up a one-way road if there's no other route, but only at a crawl, so they plan around it. A bot stuck in a solid jam for a few seconds squeezes past, so traffic never locks up for good.

Junctions and traffic lights

Where three or four roads meet, bots slow down to cross and give way to anyone already crossing the other way, so a busy crossing becomes a bottleneck. In the Paths banner choose Lights (junctions are outlined in green) and tap one to put up a traffic light for 1 Alloy. It lets one direction through at a time at full speed and switches when traffic waits the other way. On a quiet crossing it makes no difference; on a busy one it moves about half as many goods again. Tap a light to take it down and get the Alloy back.

Batteries

Every bot runs on a battery that drains as it walks, works and fights. Bots recharge inside your Command Base (three at full speed, free) or a Charging Station (four). Warbots also recharge inside their garrison. When more bots crowd in than a charger has slots, they share the power and charge slower.

Charged
Takes any job it has enough charge for, there and back.
Low · under 30%
Orange bar over the bot. It recharges as soon as it finishes its job.
Flat · under 12%
Flashing red bar. Emergency mode: half speed, and warbots hit half as hard.

If workers far from the Command Base keep running flat, or buildings say Worker is recharging, build a Charging Station near that cluster. Workers running a building step out to recharge and come straight back.

Fuel

Charging Stations burn Fuel: one Fuel recharges about three quarters of a battery, and each station keeps up to 4 in stock (workers deliver it). A station out of Fuel can't charge anyone, and its bots head for another charger or your Command Base. There are two ways to make Fuel:

  • Bio Farm. Build it within 3 tiles of fertile soil (dark, furrowed patches). Its worker plants energy crops, waits about 45 seconds for them to ripen, harvests each into one Fuel and replants. More fertile tiles in reach means steadier output. Crops never run out.
  • Oil. Build an Oil Pump right on top of an oil seep (a dark, glossy pool). It pumps Crude until the seep runs dry, and a Refinery turns each Crude into a Fuel: about 10 Fuel a minute, four times a Bio Farm, but a pump spot only holds 50 or so Crude before you have to move on. Seeps are few: one just beyond your border and a contested field in the middle of the map.

Terrain and territory

The planet has terraces at different heights: lighter ground is higher, and dark rock walls are cliffs. Bots can't climb cliffs. They use slopes (the striped ramps) at passes, so some routes wind a long way round.

  • Ramp: build one at the foot or top of a one-level cliff to open your own route up. A pass is often worth a long paved Path too.
  • You can't place a building where it would block the only way through a pass, and resources across a cliff with no route don't count as "in reach".
  • Water and rocky crags can't be crossed at all.
  • Salvage: if you run out of Stone or Fiber with no Quarry or Harvester that can still work, your Command Base's crew salvages 1 every 20 seconds (up to 6), enough to build your way back.
  • Territory: you can only build inside your border (the dashed line). The Command Base claims 8 tiles around it and each Outpost 7. If you lose an Outpost, its land goes too, and your non-military buildings left outside your border are destroyed. Gatherers only harvest on your land or unclaimed land.

War

Versus

Warbots come from the Bot Foundry and wait inside your Command Base and Outposts, filling front-line Outposts first. When enemy warbots come close, a garrison sends defenders out automatically. Buildings regain armor once they've gone about 8 seconds without being hit.

Attack a building

Tap Army, then a rival building, choose how many warbots and tap Send warbots. They come from garrisons within 14 tiles of the target, and each garrison keeps one at home. Ordinary buildings are wrecked. Outposts become yours, along with their land. Capture the rival's Command Base to win.

Station warbots in a garrison

New warbots go to whichever Outpost or Command Base needs them most, nearest the front first. Tap one of your Outposts or your Command Base to steer that. Garrison priority (Low, Normal, High) decides where new warbots, and ones called back from a rally flag, go: High garrisons fill first, Low ones last. Station here brings the number you choose from your other garrisons (each keeps one at home); they march over and stay until you move them. An Outpost holds 10 warbots and the Command Base 40.

Hold an area

Tap Army, then open ground. Your warbots march there and plant a rally flag. They fight enemy bots that come near and attack enemy buildings within 3 tiles of the flag. Bots with a flat battery walk to the nearest garrison to recharge, then come back. Tap the flag to send more or call them all home.

Missiles

A Missile Factory builds each Missile from 2 Alloy, 1 Chip and 1 Fuel, taking 20 seconds, and haulers load them into a Missile Silo (it holds two and reloads in 25 seconds). To fire, tap your Silo and press Aim missile: the map zooms out and its 18-tile range shows as a red ring on the ground. Tap any spot inside it, a rival building or open ground where enemy warbots are massing, to see the blast radius and flight path, then tap Fire (or tap the same spot again). You can also tap Army, then a rival building, then Fire missile. A hit does 24 damage, which wrecks most buildings outright (turrets, factories, even another Silo), and the blast does 5 damage to other rival buildings and 9 to bots within about 2 tiles. Outposts and the Command Base drop to almost no armor instead, so send warbots right behind the missile to capture them. Missiles are expensive, so save them for turret lines, Outposts and the Command Base. When the rival fires at you, a flashing red ring shows where it will land. The rival saves up for missiles too once its colony is going, and aims them at your turrets and Outposts first.

Ammo

Every warbot carries 20 shots. Each hit uses one, and a warbot reloads inside your Command Base or an Outpost, 10 shots per Ammo. Haulers keep each garrison stocked (Command Base 10, Outposts 6) from an Ammo Plant. A warbot with no ammo can't fight at all: it drops out of the fight and heads back to a garrison to reload (one holding a rally flag reloads and returns), and only armed warbots answer attack orders, rally flags and garrison sorties. A small brass bar under a warbot means it's running low.

Ordering bots

The Bot Foundry only builds the bots you order. Tap it, then press +1 or +5 next to Workers or Warbots; Clear cancels that queue. Mixed orders take turns. With nothing queued it sits idle and leaves your Alloy and Chips in storage.

Pulse Turrets near your Command Base and Outposts wear down raids, as long as they get Crystal. Missiles are the best way to deal with a rival turret line before your warbots walk in.

Missions

Tap Missions on the main menu. Each mission is a hand-picked planet with its own goals, starting conditions and features. Pick Easy, Normal or Hard: harder levels raise the goals, tighten the clock, start you with fewer goods and bring a tougher rival. The goal banner shows your progress and any time left.

  1. TouchdownColony. Build a Harvester, Quarry and Smelter and make your first Alloy.
  2. Assembly LineColony. Make Chips and order new bots from the Foundry.
  3. Green FuelColony. No Fuel left: grow it at a Bio Farm and keep two Charging Stations running.
  4. Rush HourColony. A far-off depot and heavy traffic: order more Haulers, lay roads with one-way lanes and put up traffic lights.
  5. BlacktopColony. Make Cement, lay roads, and upgrade them to asphalt using the oil seep beside your base.
  6. Border DisputeVersus. Capture rival Outposts and hold a share of the land.
  7. Supply LinesVersus. Your warbots land nearly empty: make Ammo and capture the rival Command Base.
  8. Final DescentVersus. A deep canyon world and a veteran rival. Capture its Command Base.

Unlock codes. Finishing a mission unlocks the next one and shows its code (like ABC-123). Type it under Have an unlock code? in the Missions menu on another phone or browser to unlock that mission there too.

Statistics

Open Statistics from the pause menu at any time, or from the end-of-game screen. You get totals, then graphs over time of your bots, the land you hold and any good you pick, with the rival's line beside yours in Versus. Drag a finger across a graph to read exact values.

How busy your buildings were ranks every kind of building by the share of the time it spent working. A busy one (near 100%) is a bottleneck worth doubling; a quiet one is waiting on inputs, workers or pickups. Tap a bar to see that building type's busy time over the game. Each building's own panel also shows how busy it has been in the last few minutes.

Status messages

Tap any building to see its status. Here's what the common ones mean and what to do.

It saysWhat to do
Needs a workerAll free workers are busy. Make more at the Bot Foundry, or pause a less useful building.
Worker is rechargingIts worker stepped out to charge. If it happens a lot, build a Charging Station nearby.
Waiting for Ore (or another good)That input isn't arriving. Check you have the building that makes it and some free workers.
Storage full / Output full, waiting for pickupNobody is free to carry goods away, or no storage accepts that good (check storage switches).
No ore veins left in reachThe deposit is used up. Demolish it and build again near fresh resources, or expand.
Waiting for materials / a builderThe site's materials are short or workers are busy. Raise its priority to jump the queue.
Idle: tap it to order botsThe Foundry has nothing queued. Tap it and press +1 or +5.
Bot limit reachedYou have 90 bots (150 in Colony). That's the maximum.
That would block the only way through herePick another spot. Buildings can't plug a pass or the foot of a slope.
Your bots cannot reach this spotIt's on a level with no slope from yours. Find a slope, or build a Ramp at a one-level cliff.
Short on workers: a worker was moved to haulingThe game freed a worker so goods keep moving. Build more workers.
Out of Fuel: bots can't charge hereThe Charging Station needs Fuel. Build a Bio Farm on fertile soil, or an Oil Pump and Refinery, and check workers are free to deliver it.
Crops are ripeningEvery fertile tile in reach is planted. The farmer harvests as soon as a crop turns pink.
No fertile soil free in reachPaths or buildings cover the soil, or there's none within 3 tiles. Move the farm or clear the soil.
The oil seep has run dryDemolish the pump and build one on another seep.
Needs an Agribot / a Paver: order one at the Bot FoundryOnly that robot type can run this building. Tap the Foundry and order one.
Waiting for AsphaltThe Roadworks is out. Build an Asphalt Plant (it needs Crude from an Oil Pump).
Every path in reach is asphaltIts job is done. Lay more paths within 7 tiles, or build another Roadworks elsewhere.
Your warbots are out of AmmoBuild an Ammo Plant and keep workers free to stock your Command Base and Outposts.

Saving and settings

  • The game saves itself every 20 seconds and whenever you leave. Continue on the main menu picks up where you left off. There's one save slot, so starting a new game or mission replaces it. Mission progress is kept separately on each device.
  • The speed button cycles 1×, 2× and 3×. The pause menu has sound on/off, a short How to play, and Save & quit.
  • Map settings and the minimap's hidden/shown state are remembered on each device.
